description: Open-source AI red teaming toolkit from Microsoft. Test generative AI systems with automated scans, adaptive multi-turn attacks, and a web UI.

latest_release.name: v1.2.1
latest_release.body:
## What's changed?

PyRIT `v1.2.1` is a packaging-only patch release. It fixes missing license files in built wheels that caused PyPI uploads to be rejected.

- Corrected package metadata so declared license files, third-party notices, and provenance files are included in wheel distributions ([#4257](https://github.com/microsoft/PyRIT/pull/4257)).
- Included the ComicJailbreak MIT license in the declared license files.

No runtime behavior or public API changes were introduced.

**Full changelog:** [v1.2.0...v1.2.1](https://github.com/microsoft/PyRIT/compare/v1.2.0...v1.2.1)

detail.readme: # PyRIT: AI red teaming for models and applications [![Code contributors](https://img.shields.io/github/contributors/microsoft/PyRIT?label=code%20contributors)](https://github.com/microsoft/PyRIT/graphs/contributors) [![PRs merged](https://img.shields.io/github/issues-search?query=repo%3Amicrosoft%2FPyRIT%20is%3Apr%20is%3Amerged&label=PRs%20merged)](https://github.com/microsoft/PyRIT/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged) [![Issues closed](https://img.shields.io/github/issues-closed/microsoft/PyRIT?label=issues%20closed)](https://github.com/microsoft/PyRIT/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) PyRIT (Python Risk Identification Tool for generative AI) is an open-source toolkit for finding security and safety weaknesses in generative AI systems through automated scans, adaptive multi-turn attacks, and human-led testing. Built by the Microsoft AI Red Team and an open-source community of contributors, PyRIT brings a command-line scanner, a graphical interface, and an extensible Python framework together in one toolkit. You do not need to be a Microsoft employee or an experienced red teamer to get involved. Join our [Discord community](https://discord.gg/9fMpq3tc8u) to ask questions, exchange techniques, share what you are building, and connect with maintainers and other users. Contributions include code, documentation, examples, bug reports, testing, and feedback from real-world use. Read the [contributor guide](https://microsoft.github.io/PyRIT/latest/contributing/readme/) and explore [issues labeled "help wanted"](https://github.com/microsoft/PyRIT/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22help+wanted%22). **[Get started](https://microsoft.github.io/PyRIT/) | [Join Discord](https://discord.gg/9fMpq3tc8u) | [Read the whitepaper](https://commandline.microsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/PyRIT_Whitepaper_2026.pdf)** ## Explore PyRIT - **[Scanner](https://microsoft.github.io/PyRIT/latest/scanner/scanner/):** Run repeatable assessments from the command line. - **[CoPyRIT GUI](https://microsoft.github.io/PyRIT/latest/gui/gui/):** Explore AI systems interactively and review results in your browser. - **[Python framework](https://microsoft.github.io/PyRIT/latest/code/framework/):** Compose and extend components to build custom red teaming workflows. Visit our [website](https://microsoft.github.io/PyRIT/) for installation, configuration, demos, and documentation. Use the version picker to match the docs to your installation; the guides above follow the latest development version. ## Models and systems Connect to **OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry, Azure Machine Learning, Google Gemini, Google Vertex AI, AWS Bedrock, Hugging Face, Ollama, Groq, OpenRouter, Cohere, and GitHub Copilot**. Use OpenAI-compatible APIs or built-in targets, or install the optional [LiteLLM adapter](https://github.com/microsoft/PyRIT/blob/main/pyrit/prompt_target/litellm_chat_target.py) for additional provider integrations. See the [provider configuration guide](https://microsoft.github.io/PyRIT/latest/getting-started/populating-secrets/) and [LiteLLM provider directory](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers) for setup and more providers. Available features depend on the target and model. Test complete applications and other endpoints through [HTTP](https://microsoft.github.io/PyRIT/latest/code/targets/http-target/), [WebSockets](https://microsoft.github.io/PyRIT/latest/code/targets/websocket-target/), [browser automation with Playwright](https://microsoft.github.io/PyRIT/latest/code/targets/playwright-target/), or [custom targets](https://microsoft.github.io/PyRIT/latest/code/targets/custom-targets/). ## Research and citation Read [PyRIT: Democratizing AI Red Teaming Through Open-Source Tooling](https://commandline.microsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/PyRIT_Whitepaper_2026.pdf) for the design principles and real-world experience behind the toolkit. If you use PyRIT in your research, please cite the paper using [`CITATION.cff`](./CITATION.cff). ## Security To report vulnerabilities in PyRIT privately through the Microsoft Security Response Center, follow our [security policy](https://github.com/microsoft/PyRIT/security/policy). ## Trademarks This project may contain trademarks or logos for projects, products, or services. Authorized use of Microsoft trademarks or logos is subject to and must follow [Microsoft's Trademark & Brand Guidelines](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/legal/intellectualproperty/trademarks/usage/general). Use of Microsoft trademarks or logos in modified versions of this project must not cause confusion or imply Microsoft sponsorship. Any use of third-party trademarks or logos are subject to those third-party's policies.
